messages.subject: ME/7104/25 — CMA mark-up of draft undertakings
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Mr Osei,

Please find attached the case team's mark-up of the draft undertakings. The principal changes are: (i) the initial divestiture period is reduced from six to four months (extendable to six in exceptional circumstances); (ii) the Monitoring Trustee proposal deadline is tightened to ten working days; and (iii) we have added an up-front buyer provision at paragraph 4. We'd be grateful for your client's response.

Regards
Lydia Cho

messages.snippet: Sarah — CMA mark-up in. The four-month divestiture window is tight but workable given Birchall Stone
messages.subject: FW: CMA mark-up of undertakings — our read
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah — CMA mark-up in. The four-month divestiture window is tight but workable given Birchall Stone tell us two trade buyers are already sniffing around the Aqualis line. The up-front buyer point is more significant — it means we can't complete the broader integration until a CMA-approved purchaser is locked. I think we accept (i) and (ii) and push back gently on (iii) to allow a fixed long-stop rather than an open-ended up-front-buyer requirement. Thoughts before I revert to the case team?

James

James Osei

messages.subject: RE: FW: CMA mark-up of undertakings — our read
messages.plaintextBody:
Agree. Accept (i) and (ii). On (iii), don't die in a ditch — the CMA almost always gets the up-front buyer where the divested business is small and there's purchaser uncertainty. Propose the long-stop wording but signal we'll accept the up-front buyer if they insist. Get it to the board with a clear recommendation. Sarah
